title: Rapid coordination of effective learning by the human hippocampus: intracranial EEG during scene recognition with eye tracking
description: Stereo-EEG recordings from six patients with medically refractory epilepsy performing a scene recognition memory task with concurrent EyeLink eye tracking. The task comprised study and gaze-contingent recognition test phases across up to eight blocks per participant. The data are a lossless iEEG-BIDS re-packaging of the authors' Zenodo release, supporting investigation of hippocampal coordination of learning and memory-guided eye movements.
methods_description: Nihon Kohden amplifier recordings at 1-2 kHz with AD-TECH depth electrodes, with eye movements recorded at 500 Hz using an EyeLink 1000. Participants studied 24 natural scenes per block and then judged repeated versus novel scenes under gaze-contingent viewing. Nihon Kohden ASCII exports were converted losslessly to BrainVision INT_32 format without filtering or re-referencing.
